reason: Selected methods, baselines and results support archive-based search with explicit benchmark-reuse limitations.

candidates.title: Keep viable earlier harness variants as search parents
candidates.rule: During self-modifying coding-agent search, compare retaining an archive of working variants with keeping only the latest working variant; allow exploration from temporarily weaker parents.
candidates.passage: only the most recent agent is retained, so a poorly performing self-modification makes subsequent improvements harder to achieve
candidates.finding: DGM outperforms its no-open-ended-exploration baseline on SWE-bench and Polyglot. The best lineage includes performance dips, illustrating that discarding weaker variants can lose useful paths.
candidates.conditions: Eighty iterations; archive admission requires compilation and continued code-editing functionality. Selection balances score and underexplored lineages.
candidates.limitations: The baseline is latest-working retention, not a comparison against every best-only or diverse-search policy. Staged and reused benchmark subsets guide selection; they are not untouched final tests. Fixed search machinery and frozen foundation models limit RSI claims.
candidates.validation_test: At matched search spend compare latest-only, best-only and archive policies. Track viable descendants and evaluate selected agents on unseen repositories or tasks.

candidates.title: Test inherited harness improvements before paying to rediscover them
candidates.rule: When changing a coding-agent backbone or task family, evaluate a previously improved harness against the minimal baseline before assuming it must be evolved again from scratch.
candidates.passage: The superior performance of DGM-discovered agents can be transferred
candidates.finding: A harness searched with Claude 3.5 Sonnet improves over the base agent when used with o3-mini and Claude 3.7 Sonnet on the reported SWE-bench subset. Cross-benchmark and language transfer are also reported. The recommendation to test inheritance first is inferred.
candidates.conditions: Transfer changes the frozen underlying model while retaining evolved tools and workflow.
candidates.limitations: Some source numbers differ between plotted labels and prose; do not rely on a precise transfer effect without checking artifacts. Transfer success in this study does not imply all heuristics transfer or remove workload-specific evaluation.
candidates.validation_test: Compare minimal, inherited and newly tuned harnesses on fresh target tasks under the new model; report quality, cost and regressions, including the tuning spend.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
